name: APM Observability Layer
description: Defines how the system is observed in operation: instrumentation and telemetry configuration, metrics, spans and traces, logs, alerts, dashboards and service-level objectives, with the resources and attributes that describe them (OpenTelemetry 1.0). Logging, metrics and tracing code, exporters and alerting rules are evidence for elements here. Modelling rules: a resource identifies the producing entity: it aggregates the instrumentation scopes running in it, maps to the application component it describes and references its node and system software. A scope aggregates the spans, metric instruments and log records emitted under it, which inherit the resource through it; a span composes its events and aggregates its links. Trace, metric and log configurations (providers) depend on the resource they are built with and aggregate their processors and exporters; they configure telemetry and do not emit, serve or monitor it. An instrumentation configuration monitors the library or code it instruments and references the scope it emits under. Each signal flows through its own processors to exporters, and an exporter accesses the storage it writes to and is served by the technology service it sends to; signals of different kinds are correlated by references (a log record to its span, a metric's exemplars to spans, a span link to its span), not by flow. Only signals and instrumentation configurations monitor elements in other layers; alerts and dashboards monitor signals, and a dashboard references the alerts it shows. Telemetry reaches the business layer only through business KPIs, metric instruments that monitor business processes and services; a metric that tracks an outcome measures it, and telemetry satisfies requirements and constraints.
